title: Kconfig: No MIN < MAX constraint on CSMA backoff range
description: LICHEN_TDMA_CONTENTION_BACKOFF_MIN_MS (range 10-5000) and LICHEN_TDMA_CONTENTION_BACKOFF_MAX_MS (range 10-10000) can be configured with MIN >= MAX (e.g., MIN=5000, MAX=100). The help text says 'uniform random in [min_ms, max_ms)' - an invalid/empty range would cause undefined behavior in the random selection code (modulo by zero or negative, wraparound, or always selecting MIN).
notes: DUPLICATE of project-LICHEN-worker6-pnel — same BACKOFF_MIN/MAX inverted range issue. Consider closing one.
close_reason: No-defect (premise false, verified): the bead claims MIN>=MAX causes UB 'in the random selection code' — no such code exists. CONTENTION_BACKOFF_MIN/MAX_MS have zero consumers in any language (C/Rust/Python): no CONFIG_LICHEN_TDMA_CONTENTION_BACKOFF_* references, no link.h macro references; only the two definition sites (Kconfig:222-243, link.h:91-92) match. The real engine (lichen/subsys/lichen/link/csma.c:39-77) uses binary exponential backoff (uniform draw over 2^exponent * 10ms unit, exponent<=5, overflow-guarded with -EOVERFLOW at csma.c:72) — it never reads these symbols, so no modulo-by-zero/negative/wraparound path is reachable. Dup pnel already closed pointing here. Real finding filed instead: dead config + help text misdocumenting the algorithm (new bead, discovered-from this one) with wire-or-remove options; adding a BUILD_ASSERT for unconsumed symbols would be ceremony, and deletion is owner-signoff territory (public macros, spec/02a references). No files touched this round -> 3x codereview passes N/A (nothing to review).
